page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance from the c2d family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. This configuration provides 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, backed by 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, its multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench is weak, falling into the bottom 25%, which is a direct consequence of its limited 2-vCPU allocation. Memory bandwidth tests show poor to weak results, particularly for small-block cached reads and large-block uncached operations. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET performance, and software compilation benchmarks score in the bottom 10%, indicating that the instance is constrained under heavy concurrent or I/O-intensive workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highmem-2 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on dedicated AMD EPYC hardware, making it a viable entry-point option for memory-sensitive tasks that do not require massive parallel compute. It is best suited for lightweight workloads requiring a larger memory footprint than standard general-purpose instances, such as small-scale web serving, basic text processing, single-threaded data compression tasks, or running lightweight background utilities. It is not recommended for database hosting, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or high-throughput real-time transactional systems.
